episode.title: Wrap terminal markdown-table content using Unicode display widths
episode.before: At parent a2174751de2e25c0f8b9ea4540c15cc1fcfba9c6, the table renderer measured processed plain-text lengths, proportionally scaled columns to the terminal width, and truncated over-width cells by JavaScript string index before appending an ellipsis. Each logical header or data row produced exactly one terminal line. Long headers and cells therefore lost content, and string-index truncation was not aligned with terminal display cells for emoji and East Asian scripts.
episode.after: At 49533cd106a646d0a80da16efaf45e00d9efe108, the renderer converts content to styled characters, measures terminal display width and widest words, allocates content width within the terminal budget, wraps headers and cells into display-width-bounded lines, tightens columns to their widest resulting line, and renders every logical row as aligned visual rows padded by measured display width. Bold header delimiters are removed before wrapping because header styling is supplied by the renderer. Tests and snapshots cover long, mixed-length, punctuation-heavy, bold-header, emoji, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and complex multi-line content.
episode.diff: The implementation replaced plain-length proportional scaling and ellipsis truncation with a memoized constraint/allocation/wrapping pipeline based on Ink styled-character width primitives; added multi-line row rendering and header-marker normalization; upgraded the Ink dependency from 6.4.8 to 6.4.10; and added 10 test scenarios plus updated snapshots demonstrating preserved wrapped content and Unicode-aligned borders.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 49533cd106a646d0a80da16efaf45e00d9efe108 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 18240 and has parent a2174751de2e25c0f8b9ea4540c15cc1fcfba9c6.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0], parent_commit, and git show --format=fuller 49533cd106a646d0a80da16efaf45e00d9efe108

evidence_units.claim: The change modifies the table renderer, its tests and snapshots, and upgrades Ink from 6.4.8 to 6.4.10; the commit reports 619 insertions and 91 deletions across six files.
evidence_units.source: git show --stat --no-renames 49533cd106a646d0a80da16efaf45e00d9efe108; package.json, packages/cli/package.json, and package-lock.json diff

evidence_units.claim: The parent renderer derived widths with getPlainTextLength, proportionally scaled them, truncated over-width strings using substring and binary search, appended an ellipsis, and rendered one line per logical row.

The new calculateWidths operation converts text to styled characters and uses styledCharsWidth, wordBreakStyledChars, and widestLineFromStyledChars to obtain display-cell content width and widest-word width.

For each column, the renderer derives minimum and maximum width constraints from the header and all cells, subtracts borders, padding, and a table margin from terminalWidth, preserves short columns when feasible, and distributes scarce or surplus width across the remaining columns.

Headers and cells are converted to styled characters, wrapped to their allocated display width, converted back to strings, and cached with measured line widths; final columns are tightened to the widest wrapped line plus padding.
Each logical row is rendered as as many visual rows as its tallest wrapped cell, with missing lines represented by empty measured cells so borders and columns remain aligned.

Bold delimiters are stripped from headers before measurement and wrapping because the renderer applies bold styling itself, preventing delimiters from being split across wrapped lines or displayed literally.
The component contract retains headers, rows, and terminalWidth as runtime inputs, so the behavioral change remains localized behind the existing table-rendering interface.
evidence_units.source: git show a2174751de2e25c0f8b9ea4540c15cc1fcfba9c6:packages/cli/src/ui/utils/TableRenderer.tsx lines 12-25; git show 49533cd106a646d0a80da16efaf45e00d9efe108:packages/cli/src/ui/utils/TableRenderer.tsx lines 21-25 and 51-55

evidence_units.claim: New component tests exercise wrapping for one long cell, all-long columns, mixed long and short columns, punctuation-heavy text, and a large table containing long headers, paragraphs, explicit newlines, and short metadata columns.
Parameterized tests render emoji and Chinese, Japanese, and Korean text in several combinations and assert representative content remains present before snapshot comparison.
Dedicated tests assert that literal bold markers are absent while header text remains present, including when a long bold header wraps.
Updated snapshots show long content preserved across multiple aligned visual rows, long headers wrapped instead of ellipsized, and emoji and East Asian content surrounded by aligned table borders.

The supplied checkout's working tree has all tracked files deleted and no Node executable is available, so the tests could not be executed during extraction; validation evidence is limited to committed tests and their expected snapshots.

candidate_atomics.name: derive-display-width-column-budget
candidate_atomics.title: Allocate column widths from terminal display-cell constraints
candidate_atomics.description: Measure headers and cells in terminal display cells, establish per-column minimum and desired widths, and allocate the available terminal budget while retaining short columns when feasible.

semantic_action.intent: Give every table column a width budget based on what the terminal occupies rather than JavaScript string length, without exceeding the width available after structural overhead.
semantic_action.pre_state: Columns are sized from plain-text lengths and proportionally scaled, which does not provide a display-cell-aware minimum derived from words and Unicode content.
semantic_action.post_state: Each column has an allocated content width derived from display-cell measurements, widest-word constraints, terminal width, borders, padding, margin, and short-column preservation rules.
semantic_action.validation: Render constrained tables containing long text, emoji, and East Asian scripts; snapshots must show stable column borders within the supplied terminal-width layout and retain short metadata columns where feasible.

candidate_atomics.name: wrap-and-align-multiline-table-cells
candidate_atomics.title: Wrap cells into aligned multi-line terminal rows
candidate_atomics.description: Wrap styled content to its allocated display width, cache each visual line's measured width, tighten columns to actual wrapped content, and expand logical rows into aligned visual rows instead of truncating content.

semantic_action.intent: Preserve over-width table content while keeping borders, padding, and neighboring cells aligned across every wrapped line.
semantic_action.pre_state: An over-width cell is truncated with substring and an ellipsis, and every logical row is restricted to one terminal line.
semantic_action.post_state: Every cell is represented by display-width-bounded visual lines; a logical row has the height of its tallest cell, shorter cells receive empty continuation lines, and padding uses cached display width.
semantic_action.validation: Component assertions must retain text from long cells, and snapshots must show complete content split across aligned visual rows for mixed lengths, punctuation, explicit newlines, emoji, and East Asian scripts.

candidate_atomics.name: normalize-renderer-owned-header-style
candidate_atomics.title: Remove redundant header markup before wrapping
candidate_atomics.description: Strip bold delimiters that duplicate renderer-owned header styling before measuring and wrapping header content.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent renderer-owned header styling markers from being displayed or split across wrapped header lines.
semantic_action.pre_state: Header strings can contain bold delimiters even though the table renderer already renders headers in bold; wrapping can separate or expose those delimiters.
semantic_action.post_state: Header measurement and wrapping operate on visible header text, while bold and color styling are applied structurally by the renderer.
semantic_action.validation: Render ordinary and wrapped bold-marked headers; output must omit literal double-asterisk markers, retain the header text, and match aligned snapshots.

candidate_workflows.name: replace-terminal-table-truncation-with-unicode-aware-wrapping
candidate_workflows.title: Replace lossy table truncation with Unicode-aware wrapping
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for terminal tables that lose long content or mismeasure emoji and East Asian text: establish a display-cell width contract, allocate columns within structural overhead, normalize renderer-owned header markup, wrap content, render aligned continuation rows, and verify representative snapshots.

workflow_graph.goal: Preserve complete markdown-table content in a bounded terminal while maintaining display-cell-correct columns and borders for ASCII, emoji, and East Asian scripts.
when_to_use: A terminal table truncates long headers or cells even though vertical wrapping is acceptable.
Column widths or padding are computed from code-unit or plain string length and become unreliable for emoji or wide scripts.
The renderer receives an explicit terminal-width budget and owns table borders, padding, and row layout.
anti_goals: Do not change the semantic contents of table cells merely to make them fit.
Do not optimize for a fixed character count when terminal display width is the relevant invariant.
Do not remove inline rendering or renderer-owned header styling.
Do not introduce horizontal scrolling or widen the terminal as a substitute for bounded wrapping.
not_applicable_when: The output surface does not have terminal display-cell width semantics.
The product explicitly requires ellipsis truncation or a single-line row contract.
No terminal-width budget or equivalent layout constraint is available.
The text system cannot preserve styling through measurement and wrapping and no compatible styled-character adapter exists.
inputs: table border, separator, padding, and margin overhead
display-cell-aware styled-character measurement and wrapping primitives
representative ASCII and Unicode rendering cases
workflow_graph.entry_state: The table fits columns by scaling measured text widths but truncates cells to one line, risking content loss and incorrect Unicode display-cell accounting.
workflow_graph.exit_state: All cells are measured and wrapped using terminal display width, logical rows expand into aligned continuation lines, renderer-owned header markup is not exposed, and committed assertions and snapshots cover long and Unicode content.

steps.condition: The table has a finite terminal-width budget and may contain content wider than that budget.
steps.validation: Calculated widths account for borders, padding, margin, widest words, full content widths, and display-cell widths rather than code-unit counts.

steps.condition: Header input may include markup for styling that the table renderer already applies structurally.
steps.validation: Literal header markers are absent from both ordinary and wrapped output while visible text and structural styling remain.

steps.condition: One or more headers or cells exceed their allocated display width, or Unicode content requires display-width-aware padding.
steps.validation: Long content remains present, each line fits its allocation, shorter sibling cells receive blank continuation lines, and snapshots show aligned borders for ASCII and Unicode cases.

validation_ladder: Unit-level assertions confirm representative fragments from long content remain instead of being ellipsized.
Header tests confirm redundant bold markers are absent before and after wrapping.
Snapshot tests verify wrapping and border alignment for single-long, all-long, mixed-length, punctuation-heavy, and complex multi-paragraph tables.
Unicode snapshots verify emoji and Chinese, Japanese, and Korean text retain content and display alignment.
Run the focused TableRenderer test suite in a materialized checkout with the pinned dependency versions; this execution remains deferred in the supplied environment.
stop_conditions: Stop if the caller requires single-line truncation rather than content preservation.
Stop if terminal display-cell measurement primitives are unavailable and cannot be introduced within scope.
Defer promotion if long-content preservation or Unicode border alignment lacks a deterministic rendering oracle.
Stop if the structural overhead alone consumes the terminal-width budget; the inspected change does not establish behavior for that pathological case.
unresolved_or_deferred: Focused tests were not executed because the supplied worktree contains tracked-file deletions and the environment lacks Node.

The committed tests demonstrate selected emoji and East Asian examples but do not establish exhaustive grapheme-cluster, combining-mark, zero-width-joiner, or pathological ultra-narrow-terminal behavior.
The implementation uses a simple regular expression for bold header normalization; nested or unmatched markdown emphasis is outside the evidenced contract.

unresolved_questions: Whether the pinned focused test suite passes when executed in a clean, dependency-installed checkout remains unverified in this extraction environment.
Behavior when available width is too small for borders and padding, or when scaled minimum widths floor to zero before the wrapping code clamps them to one, is not directly tested.
The evidence supports one issue-level workflow only; no cross-project Resolution Pattern is promoted or claimed.
